title: A plasma-ratio search identifies exploratory Alzheimer case-label associations
summary: An SVM-guided search selected plasma-protein ratios associated with Alzheimer case labels in 60 stored donor samples. Candidate combinations included KYNU/MSR1, NCAN/PRTG and IL-5Rα/GFRα-1. The groups differed in average age by about 13 years, and the search reused the evaluation data; this is not independent diagnostic validation.
ai_technology: Linear support vector machine; feature-subset search
organization: University of Massachusetts Lowell; Bedford VA Healthcare System

source_review.scope: Official primary BioC original article sections: Clinical donor metadata;preprocessing;SVM and global feature search;ratio Results and age analysis; no laboratory-method validation

evidence.ai_role: Linear SVM classification and exhaustive/forward subset search select protein ratios for separating donor-group labels; the learned selection enables the represented candidate associations.
evidence.tested: The reanalysis used 38 control and22 Alzheimer-labeled samples, with82 protein measurements generating6,642 ordered ratios. Leave-one-out scores informed selection of best subsets; observed selected-ratio differences were then examined in the same samples.
evidence.unknown: Feature search and hyperparameter selection reused the LOOCV results, so headline98–100percent separation is selection-informed and not a new independent test. Mean ages were66.5 versus79.7; adding age as another classifier input does not adjust that confounding. The source also mixes22 and23 disease-sample denominators in some results. This is a reanalysis of previously collected data, without new assays, causal protein interactions or demonstrated clinical utility.
